content.value_statement: Generic cold emails can struggle to connect with Dutch-speaking SME owners. This guide outlines a website-audit hook, a demo offer, and an opt-out.
actual_capabilities: Guides initial Dutch-language outreach for Belgian and Dutch SMEs.
Defines a demo-first approach that omits pricing from the opening email.
Suggests combining a website-audit hook with an AI-search visibility angle.
Requires an opt-out line and a single call to action.
Provides a sample subject and greeting with company and first-name placeholders.
limitations: Only the public guide and a partial example are included; the referenced complete template is absent.
No scripts are included to audit websites, verify search visibility, or send emails.
Follow-up sequences and objection handling are not included.
Response rates, deliverability improvements, and legal compliance are not independently established.

use_cases.title: Introduce a local website service
use_cases.description: Draft an initial Dutch email offering a website demo without including prices.

use_cases.title: Personalize agency outreach
use_cases.description: Use verified website observations to frame a short audit offer for a Dutch-speaking SME.

use_cases.title: Prepare a technical sales opening
use_cases.description: Connect a documented discoverability concern to an AI-search discussion and one demo request.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a first email
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a short Dutch opening email for [company] addressed to [first name]. Offer a website demo, omit pricing, and include one call to action and an opt-out.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create an initial draft from basic prospect details.

prompt_templates.title: Use a verified observation
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Dutch outreach email for [company] using this verified website observation: [observation]. Offer a demo without pricing. Include one question and an opt-out.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: personalize the opening with evidence supplied by the sender.

prompt_templates.title: Revise an existing draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Revise this email for a Dutch-speaking Belgian SME: [draft]. Remove pricing and unsupported claims. Keep one demo request and add an opt-out.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: align an existing draft with the guide.

prompt_templates.title: Combine audit and AI-search context
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft one Dutch opening email using [company], [contact], [verified website observation], and [verified AI-search evidence]. Separate facts from possibilities. Omit pricing and inspection claims beyond the evidence. Include one demo request and an opt-out.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine multiple verified inputs without overstating the findings.

best_practices: Provide verified company details and website observations before requesting a personalized draft.
Keep one demo request, omit initial pricing, and include a clear opt-out.
Review Dutch wording, factual claims, and applicable outreach requirements before sending.
anti_patterns: Claiming to have inspected a website or tested AI-search visibility without evidence.
Adding multiple competing requests, early pricing, or unsupported performance promises.
Treating an opt-out line as proof of legal compliance or permission for bulk outreach.

faq.question: What is included in this package?
faq.answer: The package contains a public guide, a demo-first framework, and a partial Dutch email example. The complete referenced template is not included.

faq.question: Who is the guide intended for?
faq.answer: It targets developers, agencies, and technical sales teams contacting Dutch-speaking SMEs in Belgium and the Netherlands.

faq.question: Does the skill inspect websites or send emails?
faq.answer: No. The included file provides writing guidance without website inspection scripts or email delivery integrations.

faq.question: Does it include follow-ups?
faq.answer: No. The guide covers initial outreach and excludes follow-up sequences and objection handling.

faq.question: Are higher response rates guaranteed?
faq.answer: No. The guide makes performance claims, but the included material provides no supporting measurements or independent validation.

faq.question: Does an opt-out make outreach legally compliant?
faq.answer: No. An opt-out alone does not establish compliance. Review applicable marketing and privacy requirements before contacting prospects.
